summary: TerraMind AI — From Orbit to Harvest is an agricultural decision-support platform powered by NASA POWER climate data. It enables users to analyze temperature and rainfall, assess crop suitability, plan crop rotations, and generate reports. By transforming complex climate data into accessible insights, TerraMind AI aims to support smarter, climate-resilient farming.
details:
Project title

TerraMind AI — From Orbit to Harvest

Selected challenge

Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data (NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026)

Short project summary

TerraMind AI is a climate-aware agricultural decision-support prototype built with NASA POWER data. Users enter geographic coordinates to explore historical temperature and rainfall, screen wheat or maize against preliminary crop climate ranges, check crop-rotation timing, and download an explainable farmer analysis report.

Problem and motivation

Farmers face changing temperatures, rainfall variability, and limited access to easy-to-interpret local climate analysis. Raw weather datasets can be hard to translate into practical questions about crop choice and planting schedules.

Solution and implementation

TerraMind AI connects a React/TypeScript dashboard to a Python/FastAPI backend. The backend retrieves historical daily NASA POWER T2M and PRECTOTCORR measurements for the selected coordinates, cleans and aggregates them using Pandas, and returns monthly climate profiles. A basic rule-based screening module compares wheat and maize requirements against historical growing-season mean temperature and annual rainfall references. A crop-rotation module checks the calendar gap between harvest and planting and whether the crop sequence stays in the same family. Users can download a text report with the values, data provenance, and explicit limitations.

Demonstrated result

For the 2025 historical climate example, Islamabad (33.7, 73.1) shows approximately 1,534.54 mm annual precipitation and a 22.64°C unweighted mean of monthly temperature means; Karachi (24.8607, 67.0011) shows approximately 365.84 mm and 26.32°C. For wheat harvest on 2027-04-25 and maize planting on 2027-05-10, the planner reports 14 full days and notes that both are cereal-family crops.

Why it matters

The prototype turns open Earth-observation data into a transparent workflow that non-specialists can explore and export. It demonstrates the foundation for future crop-planning support with local agronomic validation.

Technical stack

Python, FastAPI, Uvicorn, Requests, Pandas, React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, and Recharts.

NASA data source

NASA POWER Project — https://power.larc.nasa.gov/
Daily air temperature at 2 m (T2M) and corrected precipitation (PRECTOTCORR). The project uses historical 2025 observations; it does not claim to generate weather forecasts.

Limits and future work

The current screening is rule-based, not a trained machine-learning model or validated yield predictor. Fixed season windows and simple reference thresholds are preliminary. Site-specific soil conditions, irrigation constraints, crop variety, farmer preferences, and agronomic validation are not implemented yet. These are the next development priorities.

AI disclosure

ChatGPT and Claude were used as development and writing aids during prototyping. Source code and development history are published in the repository. This project is not affiliated with or endorsed by NASA.
